title: Component variants with variables
summary: One .btn rule reads --btn-bg and --btn-pad; .small, .danger and .ghost only change the variables.
explanation: The base .btn rule is written once in terms of variables: var(--btn-bg), var(--btn-fg), var(--btn-pad). Each variant class sets only the variables it needs. No variant repeats padding, border or radius declarations.

That keeps every variant in sync: change the border-radius in .btn and all of them follow. Combining classes also just works, since .small sets the size variables and .danger the colour ones, so a small danger button needs no extra rule.
The default values live on .btn itself, so a plain .btn looks right without any variant.
tryThis: Change --btn-radius in .btn to 999px: every button becomes a pill.
Add a .large variant that sets --btn-pad: 14px 24px and use it on a button.
Give the third button both ghost and danger classes in Items: which variable wins depends on which rule comes later.
